why: Doc sentence verified verbatim: desktop.md line 362, third bullet of the 'Claude Code applies three safety behaviors across sessions' list, single sentence, no reversing second half. Cited file:line verified: packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/send-agent-message.ts:16 is the `!ctx.sendAgentMessage` guard, and the handler really does validate only non-empty sessionId/message plus self-send. The finding fails on the third check -- the consequence. Its own load-bearing evidence is 'Our SchedulerTick automations create exactly the unwatched sessions the rule exists for, and they carry the tool', and that is false for the shipped default. Automation prompt actions create their session at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:18585 with `permissionMode: permissionMode || 'explore'`. `send_agent_message` is declared `safeMode: 'block'` (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1038), and packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2407-2422 denies every `mcp__session__*` tool absent from `getSessionSafeAllowedToolNames` (tool-defs.ts:1286-1293, which keeps only `safeMode === 'allow'`) for any mode that is not default/acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions (mode-types.ts:98-100 gate at mode-manager.ts:2160-2170). So an unattended SchedulerTick run in its default mode is already refused the tool -- enforcement one layer up from the handler, which is exactly false-positive shape #3 recorded in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md:108. The same gate blocks it in `dontAsk`, the mode this repo labels 'Unattended' (mode-manager.ts:2543). Two further scope points: our R27b scheduling primitive is session-scoped and delivers a scheduled prompt into the SAME session between turns (packages/session-tools-core/src/context.ts:428-446), so 'a scheduled-task run' has no unwatched-session counterpart on that path at all; and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md row 98 already carries the verdict WHITE / 'chuzhoy desktop-produkt' for this page. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3.
correctedState: The handler has no attendedness check, and Nessy has no attended/unattended concept at all -- but the sender half of the rule is already enforced by a different mechanism for the case the finding names. SchedulerTick prompt automations create their session in `explore` (SessionManager.ts:18585), and `send_agent_message` (`safeMode: 'block'`, tool-defs.ts:1038) is denied there and in `dontAsk` by mode-manager.ts:2407-2422. What actually remains open, and is narrower than claimed: (1) the sender block is a default, not a rule -- an automation matcher that sets `permissionMode: 'auto'` or `'bypassPermissions'` (automations/types.ts:609) produces an unwatched session that can send; (2) the recipient half is genuinely unguarded in every mode -- nothing stops a watched session from delivering into an automation session, and `listSessionsFn` (SessionManager.ts:12851-12885) filters only by status/label/search, so automation sessions are targetable.
